subject: Re: Observability add-ons — retention, tracing, dashboards (pricing & rollout)
messages:
From: Maya Gupta <maya@healthflow.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Observability add-ons pricing request (retention + tracing + dashboards)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the time on the quick intro call today. We discussed adding Redwood's observability suite to our deployment to get longer trace retention, higher-fidelity tracing, and the advanced dashboards for product analytics. Before we move to a technical POC, procurement needs ballpark pricing and a suggested rollout plan.

Quick context:
- Company: HealthFlow (consumer health workflows)
- Current Redwood usage: hosted generation API, ~50M tokens/month average across prod/test
- Observatory ask: 90-day pilot then production if results look good
- Estimated telemetry: approx 3–5 TB of trace storage monthly if we keep raw spans; ~1M traced requests/day

Please see the attached usage summary (HealthFlow_Usage_Summary.xlsx) for the last 90 days.

What we need from you:
1) Packaging options / recommended retention tiers (30d/90d/365d) and cost drivers
2) How you price traces vs. retained storage vs. dashboards (seat or ingestion model?)
3) Typical commercial concessions for pilots (credits, discounted pilot pricing) and how you structure a ramp to production
4) Any required procurement docs (MSA, SOC2 evidence) we should prepare for our security and vendor teams

We're trying to move quickly — procurement wants a reference commercial plan by EOD Friday so they can request approvals.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Gupta
Head of Platform
HealthFlow, Inc.

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-08T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons pricing request (retention + tracing + dashboards)

Hi Maya — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet, that helps. Looping Ben (commercial) for pricing and Olga (CS) for technical rollout.

High level recommendations (quick callout, more details below):
- Pilot approach: 90-day pilot with a capped ingestion allowance + 1 month of free dashboard seats. Pilot gives you data to validate retention savings and query performance.
- Pricing building blocks:
  • Trace ingestion (per-10k spans) for operational telemetry
  • Retained storage (GB-month) — tiered by age (hot/warm/cold)
  • Advanced dashboards (per-seat with a small additional storage surcharge for visual materializations)
- Commercial recommendation: tiered commitment to reduce brittleness — start with a pilot, then 12-month annual commit for production.

Questions for you (so Ben can size discounts asap):
1) Can you confirm peak QPS/day or average span size? The spreadsheet had sample rates but we need an estimate for peak day.
2) Do you require 365d full-fidelity retention or is an index+sampled archive acceptable for older data?
3) Any procurement timeline constraints beyond the Friday gate?

I'll keep this tight for procurement: see the attached draft SOW (Draft_SOW_HealthFlow.pdf) — it's a working draft for comments. I'm proposing two commercial paths below so procurement can pick which looks cleaner for approval.

Option A — Pilot-first then annual commit (recommended)
- Pilot: 90 days, up to 1.5 TB ingest cap (no charge up to cap), 3 free dashboard seats, technical onboarding included
- Production (if convert): Storage pricing at $0.35/GB-month hot; $0.12/GB-month cold; trace ingestion $12 / 10k spans; dashboards $150/seat/month
- Conversion discount: 15% off list for a 12-month commit that exceeds $75k ARR

Option B — Short ramp, higher initial discount
- Pilot: 60 days with limited sampling
- Production: same unit pricing but conversion discount 20% for 12-month commit > $150k ARR

Ben — can you confirm if either of these looks realistic on your side or whether procurement usually asks for a straight percentage off list + credits?

Next steps:
- Ben to send a concise commercial note with exact USD line items (I asked him to target tomorrow)
- Olga to confirm SOC2/KYB evidence doc links and expected timeline for onboarding

Happy to hop on a short call with procurement if that moves things faster.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — quick commercial sketch below (these are ballpark figures to help procurement run numbers; we can finalize in a quote).

Commercial sketch (USD):
- Trace ingestion: $11 per 10k spans (ingestion metered daily); expected overage billed monthly
- Retained storage (hot): $0.32 / GB-month (0-30d)
- Retained storage (warm): $0.10 / GB-month (31-365d)
- Long-term cold archival: $0.02 / GB-month (365d+) — optional tiering policy can move older data there
- Advanced dashboards: $125 / seat / month (first 3 seats included for pilots)

Pilot concessions we typically offer:
- Pilot credit: $10k platform credit applied to pilot consumption
- Free onboarding + 1 day of on-site if needed (remote is standard)
- 30% discount on dashboard seats for any pilot converted within 45 days post-pilot

Discounting guidance for production commits:
- 12-month commit > $100k ARR: 18% off list
- 12-month commit > $250k ARR: 25% off list + extended SLA options
- Custom enterprise terms available for multi-year deals (legal lead time 2–3 weeks)

Procurement notes:
- We can accept a PO to start onboarding; we will issue an initial invoice at pilot conversion unless you want a paid pilot conversion.
- If HealthFlow needs redlines, legal will need to review the MSA; DocuSign link for MSA template: https://docusign.redwood.ai/MSA-Template
I'll follow up with a compact quote PDF today.

Ben Carter
Head of Commercials | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — these numbers are helpful and directionally match our budget assumptions. A couple of asks from procurement/security before we can greenlight the pilot: 

1) Retention model — rather than raw GB-month pricing, would Redwood consider an ingestion-first model that automatically tiers to cheaper archival after N days and charges a delta for hot storage volume? That helps our forecasting because ingestion is predictable but retention can spike.
2) SOC2 + data residency evidence — we need the report or an access path for our security team (they prefer direct artifact links).
3) Shorter pilot start — procurement wants kickoff next Monday (2026-08-17). Can you commit to onboarding and a technical kickoff by EOD 2026-08-18?

If you can confirm those three things and update the SOW with an ingestion-tiered billing example, we'll put a pilot PO in train (procurement prefers a PO referencing a pilot SOW).

Procurement contact: 
- Liam Chen, Senior Procurement Manager <liam.chen@healthflow.ai>

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call Friday to lock the details.

—Maya

Maya, thanks — we can absolutely accommodate an ingestion-first model and provide the SOC2 artifacts. Quick answers and next steps below.

SOC2 & security artifacts:
- SOC2 Type II report (summary) and supporting docs are available via our secure portal. Link: https://share.redwood.ai/security/soc2 (I will send portal access to Liam).

Ingestion-first billing example (illustrative):
- Charge on ingestion: $9 / 10k spans (ingestion metered)
- Automatic tiering policy: data moves to warm after 30d, cold after 90d
- Additional hot-storage surcharge only applies when hot working set > 500 GB; surcharge: $0.15/GB-month for excess hot
- Net effect: predictable ingestion cost + bounded retention variance (we can set alerts for hot working set growth)

Timeline & immediate asks:
- SOW v2: I will update the draft SOW with the ingestion-first billing example and a pilot schedule and circulate by end of day tomorrow (2026-08-13).

- PO: If procurement can issue the pilot PO referencing the SOW (once updated), we'll provision pilot capacity within 48 hours of receiving PO.

Next steps summary:
1) Olga to share SOC2 portal access to Liam and update SOW v2 (by 2026-08-13 EOD)

Looking forward to getting started.
